question: How do steric effects of substrates and reagents influence enantioselectivity in the asymmetric electrophilic fluorination of allyl silanes and silyl enol ethers?
answer: Steric effects of substrates and reagents play a significant role in determining enantioselectivity in the asymmetric electrophilic fluorination of allyl silanes and silyl enol ethers. The presence of bulky substituents on substrates, such as at the C2 position of allyl silanes, improves enantioselectivity. For instance, when the substituent is a methyl group, the enantiomeric excess (ee) is higher compared to when the substituent is a hydrogen atom. Additionally, sterically demanding analogues of N-fluorobenzenesulfonimide (NFSI), such as N-fluoro-(3,5-di-tert-butyl-4-methoxy)-benzenesulfonimide (NFBSI), enhance enantioselectivity by weakening the reactivity of the fluorination process, leading to an improvement in enantiomeric excess by up to 18% compared to using standard NFSI.
